import HartshorneLib.Chapter4LocalTaylorExpansion

/-!
# Products of local Taylor coefficients

The Taylor coefficient of a product is the finite convolution of the
coefficients of its factors. The proof uses finite Taylor expansion and the
vanishing of coefficients below the order of a parameter power. It holds in
every characteristic and retains the specified local parameter.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace Hartshorne

open IsLocalRing
open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable section

variable {k R : Type*} [Field k] [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
  [IsLocalRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (c0 : R →ₗ[k] k)
  (hc0 : ∀ a : R, residue R (algebraMap k R (c0 a)) = residue R a)
  (t : R) (ht0 : t ≠ 0) (ht : maximalIdeal R = Ideal.span {t})

/-- Taylor coefficients transform multiplication into finite convolution. -/
theorem localTaylorCoefficient_mul (n : ℕ) (a b : R) :
    localTaylorCoefficient c0 hc0 t ht0 ht n (a * b) =
      ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (n + 1),
        localTaylorCoefficient c0 hc0 t ht0 ht i a *
          localTaylorCoefficient c0 hc0 t ht0 ht (n - i) b := by
  have h := congrArg (fun z => localTaylorCoefficient c0 hc0 t ht0 ht n (z * b))
    (eq_sum_localTaylorCoefficient_add_remainder c0 hc0 t ht0 ht (n + 1) a)
  rw [add_mul, Finset.sum_mul, map_add, map_sum] at h
  rw [mul_assoc,
    localTaylorCoefficient_parameter_pow_mul_eq_zero c0 hc0 t ht0 ht
      (Nat.lt_succ_self n), add_zero] at h
  refine h.trans (Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_)
  intro i hi
  have hin : i ≤ n := Nat.le_of_lt_succ (Finset.mem_range.mp hi)
  have hshift := localTaylorCoefficient_add_parameter_pow_mul c0 hc0 t ht0 ht
    i (n - i) b
  rw [show i + (n - i) = n by omega] at hshift
  rw [mul_assoc, ← Algebra.smul_def, map_smul, smul_eq_mul, hshift]

end
end Hartshorne
